author: Admin101
title: Seattle Event: Anarchists in the Labor Movement Panel and Discussion
content:
This event is co-sponsored by Black Rose/Rosa Negra

, 

Seattle Organized Anarchists

, and the 

Institute for Anarchist Studies

.




Anarchism emerged as a wing of the workers’ movements in the 19th century. What place do anarchists have in the contemporary labor movement?




Join us for a moderated panel and discussion with anarchists from around the Puget Sound currently engaged in the labor movement as rank-and-file workers, union staffers, and community organizers. 




How do anarchists organize in the workplace? What sets anarchists apart from other political tendencies in labor? How do anarchists relate to unions? And how can anarchists contribute to building workers power from below? 




When:

 Friday, December 4 • 6-8 PM




Where:

 Chinatown-International District, Seattle, WA (specific location details sent upon registration)







Registration is required to attend

!







Click here to register

JOMO

 is a former healthcare worker and currently organizes with immigrant workers. They write at 

https://substack.com/@chinatowncommune1312

title: Online Event: Europe in Revolt
content:
This event is organized and hosted by Black Rose/Rosa Negra (BRRN)




Hundreds of thousands have taken to the streets in France and Spain in recent weeks over issues of education and housing. As this event announcement goes up, general strikes are being prepared in both countries.




How are organized anarchists participating and strategically intervening in the upheavals?




To answer this question, we invite you to an international disucussion between members of our sibling organizations: 

Union Communiste Libertaire

, 

Liza

, and 

Embat

.




Date:

 Sunday, November 15




Time:

 9:00 AM PST / 11 AM CST / 12 PM EST / 5 PM UTC




Location:

 On Zoom, registration required







Click here to register

author: Admin101
title: Southern California Event: Towards an Anarchist History in the Inland Empire
content:
The Los Angeles Local of Black Rose/Rosa Negra announces this public event on anarchist histories of the past and present in Southern California’s Inland Empire.




Towards an Anarchist History in the Inland Empire 

will explore contemporary anarchism, especifismo, popular power, and local labor struggles and social movements in the Inland Empire.




This panel discussion features local historians Troy Andreas Araiza Kokinis, author of 

Anarchist Popular Power

, and Kevan Antonio Aguilar.




When:

 Friday November 13th • 6:30 PM




Where:

 Pain Sugar Gallery • 3635 9th St, Riverside, CA 92501




Cost:

 No cost, donations for literature accepted.

Southern California Event: Towards an Anarchist History in the Inland Empire

 appeared first on

author: Admin101
title: Sanctuary as a Verb: Experiences and Directions from Transversal Organizing for Immigrant Defense
content:
Black Rose/Rosa Negra Anarchist Federation (BRRN) is excited to announce the publication of 

Sanctuary as a Verb: Experiences and Directions from Transversal Organizing for Immigrant Defense

.




Drawing on organizing experiences of Black Rose/Rosa Negra members across the United States, this pamphlet explores how workers, neighbors, and communities are building collective resistance to ICE and defending their immigrant coworkers, classmates, and loved ones. By connecting struggles across workplaces, schools, and neighborhoods, the 

transversal organizing

 approach we prioritize builds solidarity across different sectors of society to confront the interconnected structures of domination that shape our lives.




You can find a downloadable PDF version of the pamphlet at the end of this text.







Two Years of Trump II: Immigrants in the Crosshairs, Resistance Under Attack
